title: evaluate() crashes on expressions with negative numbers
body:
Calling `evaluate` on any expression that contains a negative operand raises a `ValueError` instead of returning the result.

Steps to reproduce:

```bash
pip install pytest
python -m pytest tests/test_evaluate.py -x
```

Output:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "tests/test_evaluate.py", line 13, in test_negative_operand
    assert evaluate("2 + -3") == -1
  File "src/tinycalc/evaluate.py", line 23, in evaluate
    value = int(tokens[i + 1])
ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '-'
```

Expected: `evaluate("2 + -3")` returns `-1`.

comments.body: Confirmed on 0.1.0. The tokenizer in src/tinycalc/evaluate.py splits `-3` into `-` and `3`, so the evaluator reads the minus sign where it expects a number.
